content.thinking:
My identity length math: "sip:" (4) + "n"*240 + "@" (1) + "m"*12 + ".test" (5) = 4+240+1+12+5 = 262. To get 256: 4+240+1+6+5 = 256 → "m"*6. Host labels: "mmmmmm.test" fine. Let me set n*240 and m*6 → 256. Check host label lengths: "n"*240 label is 240 chars > 63! Invalid identity per directory... but directory identities are trusted/normalized — do they need to be valid URIs? "directory maps each canonical identity (sip:user@domain, already normalized)" — trusted; my code only does string ops on them. But `alias` lookup requires the From claim to normalize to the identity string. From `<tel:+1>` normalizes to "tel:+1" which is an alias → maps to ident. Fine regardless of identity's internal validity. But `_domain(ident)` = split at '@' → "mmmmmm.test" ✓. OK — but user label 240 chars in a *canonical identity* — is that legal? "Canonical identities also have at most 256 characters" — trusted input; no URI grammar validation required on them. Fine for the test.

Actually, to be safer let me make the identity grammar-valid too: user 63 max? USER has no length limit in the grammar. Labels ≤63: host "mmmmmm.test" ✓ valid. User "n"*240 — USER has no length constraint ✓. So ident = "sip:" + "n"*240 + "@" + "m"*6 + ".test" = 256 ✓ valid URI.

Growth: From old "<tel:+1>;tag=q7" = 15 chars; new "<"+ident+">;tag=q7" = 1+256+1+7 = 265. Wire length = 32768 - 15 + 265 = 33018 > 32768 ✓.
